title: Partner Health Review — Deck templates (Standard + Enterprise)
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact but comprehensive set of slide templates and speaker notes for recurring customer health reviews (monthly / quarterly) with two flavors: a concise Standard pack for adoption-focused mid-market accounts, and an expanded Enterprise pack for strategic, SLA-backed customers where renewal conversations require exec alignment and technical risk mitigation.

How to use this file:
- Pick the flavor that matches the audience and time allotment.
- Populate each slide with the recommended data pulls (examples below).
- Annotate speaker notes with explicit asks and next steps.
- Attach an updated renewal-tracker table as an appendix when cadence < 90 days to renewal.

Standard template (recommended length: 8–10 slides / 20–30 minutes):
1) Cover & Meeting Objectives
   - Title: Customer Checkpoint — [Customer name] | [Period]
   - Speaker notes: Remind attendees of goal: alignment on health, highlight wins, surface risks, confirm next steps.
2) Executive 30s: Status Snapshot
   - One-slide visual: traffic light health indicator (green/amber/red), NPS/CSAT trend for last 90 days, ARR band.
   - Data pulls: daily active users (DAU), average latency, core feature usage %.
3) Adoption highlights (3 bullets + screenshots)
   - Top 3 wins this period (e.g., feature X adoption, integration completed, cost-per-call reduction).
4) Metrics dashboard (single-panel with 4 KPIs)
   - Suggested KPIs: usage growth %, retention of seeded users %, error-rate by route, avg response time (p50/p95).
5) Open technical items (short list)
   - Owner, ETA, current impact. Keep to 3 items max for Standard.
6) Risk & Escalation map
   - One-liner risk score (1–5), top mitigation action, who owns the escalation.
7) Renewal snapshot & asks
   - Current ARR, renewal window, expected renewal outcome (on-track/at-risk), 2 explicit asks (budget approval, exec meeting, POC scope).
8) Next steps & owners
   - Timeboxed actions, owner, due date.

Speaker notes guidance for Standard:
- Start with a 30-second framing of the business outcome we enable.
- Use the metrics slide to tell a 2–3 bullet story: growth, friction, plan.
- Close by confirming calendar placeholders for any follow-ups and the renewal decision maker(s).

Enterprise template (recommended length: 14–20 slides / 40–60 minutes):
1) Cover & tailored agenda (list participants + roles)
2) Executive summary (1 page)
   - 2–3 sentence health narrative, renewal posture, headline asks.
3) Business impact & ROI (2 slides)
   - Quantified outcomes: time saved, cost avoided, revenue uplift tied to feature usage.
   - Suggested visualization: waterfall showing baseline vs. realized value.
4) Usage & performance deep dive (3 slides)
   - Temporal usage heatmap, model inference latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), error breakdown by route.
5) Reliability & incident review (1 slide)
   - Incidents since last review, MTTR, major mitigations, open action items.
6) Product roadmap fit and upcoming changes (1 slide)
   - Highlight features that materially affect the customer and any deprecations.
7) Security & compliance posture (1 slide)
   - Attestations, audit windows, outstanding certs, data residency notes.
8) Architecture & integration health (1–2 slides)
   - Diagram with status markers for each integration, throughput limits, and throttling events.
9) Commercial / renewal details (2 slides)
   - Contract summary, renewal triggers, price change timeline, financial rationale for upsell/discounts.
10) Risk register & mitigation plan (1 slide)
   - Risk matrix (Likelihood x Impact) and prioritized mitigations.
11) Executive ask matrix (1 slide)
   - Who we need to speak to, decisions to be made, and proposed dates.
12) Appendix: Technical appendix + audit logs (2–3 slides)
   - Query examples for the customer to validate metrics, sample SLA reports.
13) Next steps & owner calendar (1 slide)

Speaker notes guidance for Enterprise:
- Open with the business narrative: how our service ties to their critical metric(s).
- Spend time on ROI and reliability to validate commercial renewal.
- Be explicit about who must approve and when; include a single slide with names, titles, and decision dates.

Renewal tracker pattern (appendix for both flavors):
- Minimal columns: customer, ARR band, renewal date, Renewal owner (CS), Exec sponsor (customer), risk score (1–5), last engagement date, next committed meeting, ask(s), notes.
- Maintain a color-coded row-level status and a short note with the top blocking item.
- Update cadence: CS owner updates tracker after each customer touchpoint; AM/CS weekly sync to triage at-risk accounts.

Risk scoring rubric (quick):
- 1 (Low): consistent product usage, no open P1/P2s, exec sponsor engaged.
- 3 (Medium): usage drop > 20% month-over-month OR 1 open P1/P2 without ETA.
- 5 (High): major incident in last 30 days AND no executive sponsorship/contact.

Suggested visuals & data sources:
- Visuals: sparkline for usage, stacked bar for feature adoption, waterfall for ROI, small architecture diagram for integrations.
- Data sources: analytics SQL (events.user, events.request), internal telemetry (latency/error dashboards), billing reports (ARR churn pipeline), support tickets (Zendesk/Jira CS tags).

Pre-meeting checklist for CS owner:
- Verify metrics queries and screenshots are fresh (last 7 days).
- Confirm attendees and call time.
- Pre-send the 1-page executive summary to customer execs 48 hours prior.
- Attach renewal tracker snapshot to calendar invite.

Suggested facilitation script (first 2 minutes):
- "Thanks all for joining. We’ll run through a quick health snapshot, highlight wins, surface any risks, and finish with decisions and next steps. Please flag any slide where you want deeper detail; we’ve added appendix material for technical follow-ups."

Common objections and responses (cheat sheet):
- Objection: "We’re seeing higher latency than before."
  - Response: "We’ll review p95/p99 on the performance slide and propose a short-term routing change + a mid-term caching tweak; owner and ETA on the Open Tech items."
- Objection: "We need better ROI evidence."
  - Response: "We’ll pull the usage-to-revenue correlation from the last 6 months and propose a focused pilot to prove the uplift in a top account segment."

Template maintenance & ownership:
- Primary owner: Customer Success Manager (CS).
- Template steward: CS Operations (Priya Natarajan) — responsible for template updates after product changes or SLA changes.
- Quarterly hygiene: refresh KPI defaults and sample queries; align with Product on any roadmap language.

Sample timeline for renewal play (90–120 day window):
- T-120 days: health review (Enterprise) + identify internal exec sponsor if missing.
- T-90 days: commercial review with AM, draft renewal terms.
- T-60 days: executive briefing for renewals flagged as at-risk.
- T-30 days: final negotiations and contract signoff.

Quick examples of dashboard queries to include in appendix (pseudocode):
- Monthly active users by feature: SELECT feature, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) FROM events WHERE ts > date_trunc('month', current_date - interval '3 months') GROUP BY feature;
- P95 latency by route: SELECT route, percentile_disc(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY latency_ms) FROM requests WHERE ts > current_date - interval '30 days' GROUP BY route;

Version notes:
- v1.0 (2025-09-12): initial draft for Standard and Enterprise packs.
- v1.1 (2026-02-18): added risk rubric, expanded ROI visuals guidance, and renewal timeline.

Open questions / next steps for the template project:
- Should we add a light-weight 1-pager specifically for SMB accounts that can be emailed instead of presented?
- Request CS Ops to pilot this template with five at-risk accounts in March; capture outcomes and iterate.

Contact / steward:
- Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.com) — customer success template owner; comments welcome in the doc or Slack #cs-templates.
